rows.evidence: Q1: Study Area and Results sections - the authors run their own simulated-annealing/EPANET model (RASGEMINEC) on a real 191 ha citrus network with 385 hydrants in Valencia, reporting energy consumption for elevation-based sectoring (Table 1), SA-optimised sectoring (Table 3) and on-demand operation via Monte Carlo (Table 4).
rows.notes: The study only reports energy consumption and installed power outcomes of sectoring (11.7-15.5% energy saving, 21.6-38.3% less power). It does not evaluate water use, over- or under-irrigation of plots, or water-management efficiency. It does assume a single uniform irrigation time (tr = 3.29 h, computed from the July peak requirement for citrus with a uniform application rate) for all hydrants, which is the precondition the review builds on, but the claimed consequence (some plots receiving more or less water than required, inefficient water management) is the review's inference and is not measured, modelled or discussed by the study. The model outputs are also never compared with measured data from the network.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a simulation/optimisation study of pumping-energy sectoring; it contains no results on water conservation or irrigation adequacy, so the review's claim about inefficient water management is not supported by the study's own findings.
